body_markdown:
*Essential market data, adoption trends, and productivity insights showing why conversational app development through existing AI assistants is reshaping software creation*


The broader AI code assistant market was[valued at $5.5 billion](https://market.us/report/ai-code-assistant-market) in 2024, with projections reaching $47.3 billion by 2034. This growth highlights increasing demand for AI-assisted development. Platforms like[Floot's MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) enable non-technical founders to build full-stack applications through Claude or ChatGPT while Floot manages hosting, databases, authentication, and deployment.


This gap between tool usage and trusted production deployment helps explain why platforms that let builders use existing AI assistants through managed infrastructure, like[Floot's MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , offer a practical way for non-technical founders and other builders to create working applications.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Vibe coding remains limited among professional developers.** According to the 2025 Stack Overflow survey, approximately[72% of respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) did not use vibe coding in their professional workflows, despite growing adoption of AI coding tools.
- **Productivity gains vary by study and context.** Research reported improvements of[roughly 10%](https://shiftmag.dev/this-cto-says-93-of-developers-use-ai-but-productivity-is-still-10-8013/) in one dataset and[15% or more](https://menlovc.com/perspective/2025-the-state-of-generative-ai-in-the-enterprise/) in reported team velocity, while a controlled study found slower performance in a specific developer setting.
- **Trust in AI accuracy declined in the 2025 survey.** Developer trust[fell to 29%](https://stackoverflow.blog/2025/12/29/developers-remain-willing-but-reluctant-to-use-ai-the-2025-developer-survey-results-are-here/) from 40%, with 46% actively distrusting output accuracy.
- **Security testing reveals significant vulnerabilities.** Veracode's 2025 controlled tests found[45% of evaluated samples](https://www.veracode.com/blog/ai-generated-code-security-risks) introduced detectable OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities.
- **Floot connects existing AI assistants to managed app infrastructure.**[Floot's MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) lets builders create full-stack apps through Claude or ChatGPT while Floot provides hosting, databases, authentication, and other managed services.


## **The AI Code Assistant Market: Size, Growth, and Spending**


The financial scale of AI-assisted development has reached a point where code generation represents a major enterprise AI use case. Understanding these market dynamics reveals why production-grade infrastructure for AI-built apps matters more than ever.


### **1. Market valued at $5.5 billion in 2024**


The global AI code assistant market reached[$5.5 billion in 2024](https://market.us/report/ai-code-assistant-market) , establishing code generation as a significant category within software technology spending. This baseline valuation reflects growing adoption of AI-powered development tools across organizations of different sizes. The market estimate covers AI tools supporting code generation, debugging, autocompletion, and related development activities rather than vibe coding platforms alone, making it a broader market indicator.


### **2. Projected to reach $47.3 billion by 2034**


Industry projections indicate the market could grow nearly ninefold[to $47.3 billion](https://market.us/report/ai-code-assistant-market) by 2034, representing sustained expected demand for AI-powered development tools. This growth trajectory suggests code generation may become an increasingly important component of software development infrastructure rather than an optional productivity enhancement. However, the 2034 figure remains a forecast based on market assumptions rather than revenue already achieved.


### **3. Growing at 24% CAGR through 2034**


The AI code assistant sector is projected to grow at a[24% compound annual growth rate](https://market.us/report/ai-code-assistant-market) from 2025 to 2034, according to Market.us. This forecast reflects expectations of expanding market adoption and spending as organizations incorporate AI assistance into development workflows. The CAGR is a projected average annual growth rate across the forecast period, not a confirmed rate maintained in every individual year.


### **4. Code generation growing at 53% CAGR**


Within the broader generative AI market, code generation was identified as the fastest-growing sector, with a projected[53% CAGR](https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/research/generative-ai-market-revenue-projected-to-grow-at-a-40-cagr-from-2024-2029) from 2024 to 2029, surpassing other AI modalities. This exceptional forecast reflects strong commercial interest in AI-assisted coding. S&P Global also noted that software development's established productivity measurements and quality assurance practices can help organizations evaluate these tools and justify broader adoption.


### **5. AI coding spend exploded 7x in one year**


Enterprise AI coding expenditure[grew from $550 million](https://menlovc.com/perspective/2025-the-state-of-generative-ai-in-the-enterprise/) to $4.0 billion between 2024 and 2025, demonstrating rapid corporate adoption. This sevenfold increase highlights how quickly enterprise spending on AI coding tools expanded, according to Menlo Ventures' estimates. The growth included spending on code completion tools, coding agents, and AI app builders, reflecting wider use across different development activities and organizational workflows.


### **6. Coding represents 55% of departmental AI spend**


In 2025, AI coding tools accounted for[55% of departmental AI spending](https://menlovc.com/perspective/2025-the-state-of-generative-ai-in-the-enterprise/) , making coding the largest category within departmental AI applications. Menlo Ventures estimated coding expenditure at $4.0 billion out of $7.3 billion spent on departmental AI tools. This majority share indicates that software development attracted substantial enterprise AI investment compared with other departmental use cases such as marketing, customer support, and IT operations.


### **7. North America holds 38% market share**


North America accounted for an estimated[$2.0 billion](https://market.us/report/ai-code-assistant-market) in AI code assistant market revenue in 2024, representing approximately 38% of the global market. This regional concentration reflects significant demand for AI-powered development tools within North America. Market.us attributed the region's position partly to its established technology ecosystem, software development activity, and enterprise interest in tools that support coding productivity and automation.


### **8. U.S. market alone valued at $1.8 billion**


The United States AI code assistant market reached[$1.8 billion in 2024](https://market.us/report/ai-code-assistant-market) , with a projection of approximately $12.4 billion by 2034. Market.us estimated a 21.5% CAGR for the U.S. market from 2025 to 2034. These figures suggest continued expected growth in demand for AI-assisted software development across businesses, independent developers, and other users, although the long-term projection remains uncertain.


## **Developer Adoption: Who Uses AI Coding Tools and How Often**


Understanding adoption patterns reveals where vibe coding fits within professional development workflows. These statistics show the gap between general AI tool usage and actual vibe coding practice.


### **9. 84% of developers use or plan to use AI tools**


In 2025,[84% of respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) were using or planning to use AI tools in their development process, up from 76% in 2024. This result indicates widespread AI adoption and interest among surveyed developers. However, the figure combines current users with respondents planning future adoption, so it should not be interpreted as an 84% active usage rate across the entire developer population.


### **10. 73% of AI coding assistant users use them daily**


In Stack Overflow's 2026 survey,[73% of AI assistant users](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data/ai-freq) reported using coding assistants or coding agents daily. The survey also recorded 20.1% weekly use and 6.2% monthly or infrequent use within the relevant respondent group. These findings demonstrate that AI coding assistance had become a regular part of many surveyed professionals' workflows rather than being reserved solely for occasional technical questions or complex tasks.


### **11. 51% of professional developers use AI daily**


In Stack Overflow's 2025 survey,[51% of professional developers](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) reported daily AI tool usage. This majority adoption among surveyed professionals indicates that AI coding tools had moved beyond limited experimentation into regular development practice. The result reflects a survey population rather than a complete count of developers worldwide, but it provides evidence of widespread integration of AI assistance into professional coding workflows.


### **12. 90% of software professionals use AI at work**


Google's 2025 DORA research found that[90% of software professionals](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/dora-report-2025/) used AI at work, with adoption increasing from the previous year's level. The surveyed group included people in software development roles, from developers to product managers. This high reported usage indicates that AI tools had become common across several software delivery activities, although adoption frequency and practical benefits varied between individuals, teams, and tasks.


### **13. 75% use AI coding assistants weekly**


Approximately three-quarters of surveyed developers[used AI assistants weekly](https://shiftmag.dev/this-cto-says-93-of-developers-use-ai-but-productivity-is-still-10-8013/) , according to research presented at the 2026 Pragmatic Summit. The reported findings drew on survey responses from approximately 121,000 developers across more than 450 companies. Weekly engagement indicates that AI assistance had become a regular development resource for many participants, although it does not establish that every user experienced measurable productivity improvements from those tools.


### **14. 65% daily usage in top-quartile organizations**


High-performing organizations reported[65% daily AI adoption](https://menlovc.com/perspective/2025-the-state-of-generative-ai-in-the-enterprise/) among developers, compared with 50% overall, according to Menlo Ventures' 2025 research. This difference suggests that intensive AI tool usage was more common in top-quartile organizations within the reported dataset. However, adoption rates alone do not establish that AI caused superior organizational performance, since team practices, engineering processes, and other factors can influence outcomes.


## **The Vibe Coding Reality: Practice vs. Perception**


These statistics reveal a striking disconnect between AI tool adoption and actual vibe coding practice. The data suggests most developers use AI for assistance rather than full application generation.


### **15. 26,564 respondents answered the professional vibe coding question**


In the[2025 Stack Overflow survey](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) , 26,564 respondents answered the question about vibe coding in their professional work, with most reporting that they did not practice it. This substantial response count provides a useful foundation for understanding how vibe coding fits into professional development. The question specifically asked whether generating software from LLM prompts was part of respondents' professional workflows.


### **16. 72% do not vibe code at work**


The majority of respondents,[approximately 72%](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) , stated that vibe coding was not part of their professional development work in the 2025 Stack Overflow survey. An additional 5% emphatically rejected the practice. This gap between general AI tool usage and vibe coding suggests that many developers continue using AI primarily for assistance rather than relying on conversational prompts to generate entire applications.


### **17. About 5% emphatically reject vibe coding**


A portion of respondents actively rejected the practice, with[about 5% answering emphatically no](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) when asked whether vibe coding was part of their professional work. This response was separate from the approximately 72% who otherwise reported not vibe coding. The survey documents the strength of these responses but does not establish the specific motivations behind them, such as security, maintainability, or code quality concerns.


## **AI-Generated Code: Volume and Production Deployment**


The amount of code being generated by AI systems continues to grow, but questions remain about how much reaches production environments.


### **18. About 4.2 million developers featured in AI-authorship analysis**


Research discussed by[ShiftMag](https://shiftmag.dev/this-cto-says-93-of-developers-use-ai-but-productivity-is-still-10-8013/) examined AI-authored production code across approximately 4.2 million developers between November 2025 and February 2026. The findings were presented by DX CTO Laura Tacho at the 2026 Pragmatic Summit. This large-scale dataset provides insight into how frequently AI-authored changes reach production environments, although the figures should be interpreted within the research's defined measurement approach.


### **19. 26.9% of production code is AI-authored**


In an analysis covering approximately 4.2 million developers,[26.9% of production code](https://shiftmag.dev/this-cto-says-93-of-developers-use-ai-but-productivity-is-still-10-8013/) was classified as AI-authored with minimal human intervention, up from 22% the previous quarter. This quarter-over-quarter increase indicates a growing share of AI-authored code entering production within the measured dataset. However, these figures do not establish whether changes in developer confidence, review processes, or tool capabilities caused the increase.


### **20. Daily AI users merge nearly one-third of their code from AI**


Developers who used AI tools daily merged[nearly one-third](https://shiftmag.dev/this-cto-says-93-of-developers-use-ai-but-productivity-is-still-10-8013/) of their code from AI-generated output, according to research presented in February 2026. The measurement concerned code entering the main repository or production after review. This proportion highlights the extent of AI participation in development workflows among frequent users, but it does not independently establish that the resulting code consistently met quality or security requirements.


### **21. 25% of Y Combinator W25 batch had 95% AI-generated codebases**


One quarter of Y Combinator's Winter 2025 batch reportedly had[95% AI-generated codebases](https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/06/a-quarter-of-startups-in-ycs-current-cohort-have-codebases-that-are-almost-entirely-ai-generated/) , signaling startup acceptance of AI-heavy development approaches. Y Combinator's managing partner clarified that these founders were technically capable of building their products independently. The finding therefore demonstrates substantial AI code generation among technically skilled startup teams rather than proving that the participating founders lacked programming expertise.


## **Productivity Claims vs. Measured Reality**


Perhaps the most revealing statistics concern the gap between perceived and actual productivity gains from AI coding tools.


### **22. Over 80% of DORA respondents report AI productivity gains**


In Google's 2025 DORA research,[over 80% of respondents](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/dora-report-2025/) reported that AI had enhanced their productivity. This widespread perception of benefit indicates that many software professionals experienced improvements from AI assistance. However, the finding reflects respondent assessments rather than a uniform measured productivity increase, and the magnitude of reported benefits may vary across tasks, experience levels, and specific AI tool implementations.


### **23. Teams report 15%+ velocity gains with AI tools**


Teams adopting AI tools across the software development lifecycle reported[15% or greater velocity gains](https://menlovc.com/perspective/2025-the-state-of-generative-ai-in-the-enterprise/) , according to Menlo Ventures' 2025 research. These reported improvements suggest meaningful acceleration in some development workflows, including coding, testing, and related activities. However, the figures represent reported team outcomes rather than a universal productivity guarantee, and the gains may differ according to implementation, organizational processes, and the tasks being performed.


### **24. Developers report saving about 4 hours per week**


Developers[reported saving about 4 hours](https://shiftmag.dev/this-cto-says-93-of-developers-use-ai-but-productivity-is-still-10-8013/) per week using AI coding assistants, based on research presented in February 2026. This self-reported time savings corresponds to approximately 10% of a standard 40-hour workweek. However, perceived time savings should not be treated as equivalent to independently measured productivity gains, since overall output also depends on review, debugging, testing, and other development activities.


### **25. 60% report at least 25% increase in coding speed**


More than[60% of developers](https://market.us/report/ai-code-assistant-market) reported at least a 25% improvement in coding speed with AI assistance, according to figures cited by Market.us. These reported improvements suggest that many developers perceive substantial benefits from AI-powered coding tools. However, self-reported coding speed is not necessarily equivalent to measured end-to-end development productivity, which also includes reviewing, testing, debugging, and deploying completed software.


### **26. One large study reported roughly 10% productivity gains**


Research presented in 2026 reported that[productivity gains around 10%](https://shiftmag.dev/this-cto-says-93-of-developers-use-ai-but-productivity-is-still-10-8013/) had remained relatively stable during the observed period, according to DX CTO Laura Tacho's findings. This modest improvement contrasted with widespread adoption of AI coding assistants. The reported figure highlights the importance of distinguishing overall productivity changes from developer perceptions of time savings, although the research account does not establish a universal productivity gain for every team.


### **27. Experienced developers forecast 24% speed-up but measured 19% slower**


In a 2025 randomized controlled trial involving 16 experienced open-source developers, participants[predicted 24% faster completion](https://metr.org/blog/2025-07-10-early-2025-ai-experienced-os-dev-study/) but actually performed 19% slower when using AI tools. This reversal demonstrates how perceived productivity improvements can differ from measured performance in a controlled setting. However, the study concerned experienced developers working on familiar repositories with early-2025 AI tools, so its results should not be generalized to all development environments.


### **28. Onboarding time cut in half**


New developer onboarding time, measured by the time required to reach the tenth pull request,[decreased 50%](https://shiftmag.dev/this-cto-says-93-of-developers-use-ai-but-productivity-is-still-10-8013/) between Q1 2024 and Q4 2025. This reduction indicates faster onboarding within the observed period. Although AI assistance may help developers understand unfamiliar codebases, the reported figures alone do not establish that AI independently caused the improvement, since other organizational and workflow changes may have contributed.


## **Trust and Sentiment: The Confidence Crisis**


These statistics reveal a growing trust problem that affects how developers approach AI-generated code and which tools they choose.


### **29. 46% actively distrust AI accuracy**


Nearly half of respondents,[46% of developers](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) , actively distrusted the accuracy of AI tool output in Stack Overflow's 2025 survey. This widespread skepticism demonstrates that increasing AI adoption did not necessarily translate into confidence in generated results. The finding supports the importance of human verification, particularly when developers use AI-generated code in applications where incorrect behavior or security problems could have significant consequences.


### **30. Only 3% highly trust AI output**


Just[3% of developers](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) expressed high trust in AI-generated output in Stack Overflow's 2025 survey, indicating widespread caution about accuracy. This small proportion contrasts with the much larger number of respondents using or planning to use AI tools. The result suggests that frequent adoption and strong confidence are distinct measures, and developers may continue checking AI-generated results even when the tools are useful.


### **31. Trust in AI accuracy fell from 40% to 29%**


Developer trust in AI accuracy[fell from 40% to 29%](https://stackoverflow.blog/2025/12/29/developers-remain-willing-but-reluctant-to-use-ai-the-2025-developer-survey-results-are-here/) in the comparison reported by Stack Overflow for 2025. This decline occurred despite growing adoption of AI development tools. The finding indicates that increased usage did not produce a corresponding increase in confidence, although the survey comparison alone cannot establish precisely why respondents became more cautious about AI-generated answers and code.


### **32. Positive favorability decreased from 72% to 60%**


Overall positive sentiment toward AI tools[declined from 72% to 60%](https://stackoverflow.blog/2025/12/29/developers-remain-willing-but-reluctant-to-use-ai-the-2025-developer-survey-results-are-here/) between the 2024 and 2025 Stack Overflow survey results. This 12-percentage-point decrease suggests that the initial honeymoon period was ending for some developers. Although AI tools remained widely used, the change indicates more mixed attitudes toward their practical value. The figures represent historical survey sentiment rather than a verified trend continuing through 2027.


### **33. Experienced developers are most cautious**


Experienced developers showed[only 2.6% high trust](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) and 20% high distrust in AI output accuracy in the 2025 Stack Overflow survey. These results indicate particularly cautious attitudes among respondents with greater development experience. However, the association between experience and skepticism does not establish causation, and the survey does not prove that every experienced developer is less trusting than less experienced counterparts.


## **Pain Points: Where AI Coding Falls Short**


Understanding developer frustrations reveals opportunities for improvement in AI-powered development workflows.


### **34. 66% cite "almost right, but not quite" as biggest frustration**


The most common complaint, reported by[66% of developers](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) , involved AI solutions that were almost correct but still required correction. This near-miss problem can be particularly time-consuming because developers must review generated code and identify errors before making changes. The result highlights a practical limitation of AI assistance: generating plausible code is not equivalent to delivering a correct, tested, and maintainable implementation.


### **35. 45% say debugging AI-generated code is more time-consuming**


In the 2025 Stack Overflow survey,[45% of respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) cited time-consuming debugging of AI-generated code as a frustration. This debugging burden can arise when generated implementations contain logical flaws, missing edge cases, or inconsistencies requiring additional investigation. The finding shows that AI assistance can create extra verification work even when initial code generation appears fast, potentially reducing the net time saved during development.


### **36. 75.3% would still ask another person for help**


In Stack Overflow's 2025 survey,[75.3% of respondents](https://stackoverflow.blog/2026/09/30/getting-ready-for-2026-results-a-look-back-on-developer-survey-findings/) said they would still ask another person for help when they did not trust AI's answers, even in a hypothetical future where AI could perform most coding tasks. This preference indicates the continuing importance respondents placed on human judgment. However, the question measured hypothetical future preferences rather than observed current help-seeking behavior.


## **Code Quality and Security Concerns**


Security vulnerabilities in AI-generated code represent a significant risk factor that builders must address.


### **37. 45% of tested AI code samples introduced OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities**


Veracode's 2025 controlled tests found that[45% of evaluated samples](https://www.veracode.com/blog/ai-generated-code-security-risks) introduced detectable OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, with a 72% failure rate for Java and an 86% failure rate on relevant cross-site scripting tasks. These findings demonstrate security weaknesses in the tested AI-generated code. The results apply to Veracode's defined test scenarios and should not be interpreted as a measured vulnerability rate across all AI-generated production software.


### **38. Java code samples had a 72% failure rate in Veracode tests**


In Veracode's 2025 security testing,[AI-generated Java samples](https://www.veracode.com/blog/ai-generated-code-security-risks) failed security evaluations approximately 72% of the time. This was a higher failure rate than those reported for the other programming languages examined in the study. The results underscore the need for security testing when using AI assistance to develop Java applications, particularly for backend systems handling sensitive information or security-critical functionality.


### **39. 86% failure rate on tested cross-site scripting tasks**


AI-generated code showed[86% failure rates](https://www.veracode.com/blog/ai-generated-code-security-risks) on relevant cross-site scripting protection tasks in Veracode's 2025 tests, creating significant potential web security risks. Cross-site scripting vulnerabilities can arise when applications fail to handle untrusted data safely. This result indicates that the tested models frequently failed to implement appropriate protections in those scenarios, reinforcing the need for secure coding practices and independent security checks.


### **40. 88% failure rate on tested log injection tasks**


Veracode reported an[88% failure rate](https://www.veracode.com/blog/ai-generated-code-security-risks) on tested log injection tasks involving AI-generated code. Log injection vulnerabilities can allow attackers to manipulate application logs, potentially inserting misleading entries or interfering with security investigations. This particularly high failure rate in the evaluated scenarios illustrates why generated implementations should be checked for proper handling of untrusted input before they are deployed into production systems.


## **Enterprise Adoption and Market Dynamics**


Enterprise-level statistics reveal how organizations are incorporating AI coding tools into their technology stacks.


### **41. 32.8% report organizations use a few approved AI tools**


In the[2026 Stack Overflow survey](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data/ai-try) , 32.8% of respondents said their organizations used a few approved AI tools or models. This was the most frequently selected response to the question about organizational approaches to evaluating AI tools. The result indicates that standardized tool selection was common among surveyed organizations, although the question does not directly establish whether security, compliance, cost, or another consideration drove those decisions.


### **42. 76% of AI solutions are purchased, not built**


In 2025, organizations increasingly[purchased AI solutions](https://menlovc.com/perspective/2025-the-state-of-generative-ai-in-the-enterprise/) rather than building them internally, with purchased solutions accounting for 76% of reported AI use cases, up from 53% in 2024. This shift indicates greater reliance on commercially available AI products. However, the finding does not establish that internal development is generally impractical or that purchased solutions consistently provide better long-term maintenance or performance.


### **43. AI deals convert at 47% vs. 25% for traditional SaaS**


Menlo Ventures reported that[47% of AI deals](https://menlovc.com/perspective/2025-the-state-of-generative-ai-in-the-enterprise/) progressed to production, compared with 25% of traditional SaaS deals. This difference indicates a higher reported production conversion rate for evaluated AI solutions within the research. The result suggests strong buyer commitment among organizations exploring AI, although conversion rates alone do not establish long-term customer satisfaction, profitability, or sustained productivity gains after implementation.


### **44. 27% of AI app spend comes through PLG motions**


Product-led growth accounted for[27% of AI app spending](https://menlovc.com/perspective/2025-the-state-of-generative-ai-in-the-enterprise/) in 2025, compared with 7% in traditional software, according to Menlo Ventures. This higher share reflects the importance of individual users and bottom-up adoption in the AI application market. The findings indicate that AI products were frequently adopted through direct user experimentation before broader organizational procurement, although purchasing patterns vary by product category.


## **AI Model and Tool Market Share**


Understanding which AI models power coding workflows helps explain developer preferences and platform choices.


### **45. Anthropic accounted for 40% of enterprise LLM spend in 2025**


Anthropic accounted for an estimated[40% of enterprise LLM spending](https://menlovc.com/perspective/2025-the-state-of-generative-ai-in-the-enterprise/) in 2025, compared with 27% for OpenAI, according to Menlo Ventures. This distribution reflects Anthropic's substantial share of enterprise foundation model spending during the measured period. However, spending share alone does not establish which model features or purchasing considerations drove the result, and the figures should not be interpreted as current 2027 market shares.


### **46. Anthropic held an estimated 54% of enterprise coding-model share in 2025**


Menlo Ventures estimated that Anthropic held[54% enterprise coding-model share](https://menlovc.com/perspective/2025-the-state-of-generative-ai-in-the-enterprise/) in 2025, compared with 21% for OpenAI. This estimate indicates strong enterprise adoption of Anthropic's models in coding-specific applications during the measured period. However, spending share does not independently establish comparative code generation performance, and the result should not be treated as a prediction of future market leadership.


### **47. 81.7% of out-of-the-box AI assistant users selected ChatGPT**


In Stack Overflow's 2025 survey,[81.7% of respondents](https://stackoverflow.blog/2026/09/30/getting-ready-for-2026-results-a-look-back-on-developer-survey-findings/) using out-of-the-box AI assistants selected ChatGPT, demonstrating its popularity within that surveyed group. The result measures reported tool selection among respondents rather than enterprise coding-model spending or overall market share. It also does not establish why respondents selected ChatGPT, since factors such as price, familiarity, and capabilities were not directly measured by this statistic.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What exactly is vibe coding and how does it differ from traditional AI-assisted coding?**


Vibe coding involves describing an application in natural language and using AI to generate software rather than writing every line manually. Traditional AI coding assistants often provide autocompletion, debugging assistance, and code suggestions, while vibe coding can involve generating larger application components through conversational prompts. In the 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey,[approximately 72%](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) reported that they did not vibe code professionally, with another[5% emphatically rejecting](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) the practice, although[84%](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) were using or planning to use AI development tools. Platforms such as[Floot's MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) can connect conversational development to managed application infrastructure.


### **Why do productivity statistics vary so widely for AI coding tools?**


Teams reported[15% or greater](https://menlovc.com/perspective/2025-the-state-of-generative-ai-in-the-enterprise/) velocity gains according to Menlo Ventures, while a controlled study showed experienced developers working[19% slower](https://metr.org/blog/2025-07-10-early-2025-ai-experienced-os-dev-study/) with AI on familiar repositories. These differences reflect variations in research methods, developer experience, task complexity, and the workflows being measured. Perceived speed improvements may not translate to measured performance when accounting for the full development cycle, including reviewing, testing, debugging, and deployment. No single productivity figure applies universally to every developer or organization.


### **What security concerns should I consider when using AI-generated code?**


Veracode's 2025 controlled tests found that[45% of evaluated samples](https://www.veracode.com/blog/ai-generated-code-security-risks) introduced detectable OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities. Java samples had approximately[72% security failure rates](https://www.veracode.com/blog/ai-generated-code-security-risks) , while cross-site scripting protection failed in[86% of relevant tasks](https://www.veracode.com/blog/ai-generated-code-security-risks) . These results demonstrate why AI-generated code requires thorough security review before production deployment. Using managed services such as[Floot's platform infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/platform/security-and-data) can simplify parts of application setup, but it does not eliminate the need to test application code and verify its security.


### **How do enterprise coding-model market shares compare with ChatGPT usage surveys?**


Menlo Ventures estimated that Anthropic held[54% enterprise coding-model share](https://menlovc.com/perspective/2025-the-state-of-generative-ai-in-the-enterprise/) in 2025, compared with[21% for OpenAI](https://menlovc.com/perspective/2025-the-state-of-generative-ai-in-the-enterprise/) . Meanwhile, Stack Overflow's 2025 survey found that[81.7% of respondents](https://stackoverflow.blog/2026/09/30/getting-ready-for-2026-results-a-look-back-on-developer-survey-findings/) using out-of-the-box AI assistants selected ChatGPT. These figures reflect different measurement contexts: enterprise spending on coding models versus individual developer tool selection. They are not directly comparable measures of market leadership, and neither figure establishes the market shares for 2027.


### **What should non-technical founders look for in a vibe coding platform?**


Focus on platforms that support your existing AI subscription while clearly explaining plan limits, hosting charges, and optional AI-credit costs. Prioritize managed databases, authentication, storage, backend infrastructure, and deployment capabilities for working applications.[Floot's pricing](https://floot.com/pricing) provides a free-to-start option with paid plans for higher building-action limits and hosting allowances. Its[mobile app workflows](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) also support iOS and Android builds, although developer accounts and app-store approval remain separate requirements. Regardless of the platform, proper testing and security review are essential before production use.
